purpose: Named decomp-parity foundation gaps for compact runtime and replay parity work. This ledger is an index, not source truth; inspect the decomp before changing runtime behavior.
rules: Decomp is the primary source of truth; Slippi is a secondary witness.
Assign replay divergence to a decomp phase before implementing a parity change.
Keep source floats as floats through extraction, overlays, baking, and runtime.
Normal runtime consumes compact baked artifacts, not debug/sample JSON.
Devtool ECB edits resolve through source pose/rig/animation data and typed overrides, not hand-authored gameplay ECB boxes.

gaps.decomp_phase: ECB setup, JObj sampling, sanitize, bottom lock, and interpolation
gaps.known_gap: Runtime no longer emits per-frame EcbDiamond runtime samples or per-frame SourceFighterEcb source sample arrays in crates/mole_core/src/generated/falcon_ecb.rs. The live JObj evaluator is now the normal ECB source path and accepts mpColl_LoadECB_JObj flags, including the raw +/-2.0F expansion branch used by flags such as 0x12. The remaining ECB runtime size gap is that the live evaluator is still embedded as a large legacy Rust artifact instead of a compact source-backed runtime bundle. Live source pose coverage is also missing for the common ledge option batch: CliffClimbSlow, CliffClimbQuick, CliffAttackSlow, CliffAttackQuick, CliffEscapeSlow, CliffEscapeQuick, CliffJumpSlow1, CliffJumpSlow2, CliffJumpQuick1, and CliffJumpQuick2.
gaps.next_proof: Move the flag-aware live JObj ECB evaluator out of the legacy generated Rust artifact into compact runtime data, and extract/route the common ledge option action pose data from the decomp/source assets instead of relying on fallback ECB.

gaps.decomp_phase: Ground, wall, ceiling, ledge, pass-through platform, floor-skip, and connectivity collision loops
decomp_refs: common Coll callbacks in ftCommon state files
gaps.known_gap: Grounded collision has the strongest Rust coverage. Wall, ceiling, ledge, platform pass, and connectivity behavior are still incomplete relative to the decomp-shaped loops.
gaps.next_proof: Implement collision loop slices only after identifying the matching decomp helper and required state callback phase.

gaps.decomp_phase: MapCollData topology, line flags, links, surface attributes, friction, and ledge metadata
gaps.known_gap: Battlefield extraction and generated runtime data now preserve MapCollData-style topology for the first dev stage: vertex/line/joint counts, floor/ceiling/right-wall/left-wall ranges, raw line flags, ledge metadata, callbacks, and map_head data are guarded by core tests. The remaining stage parity gap is broader validation of dynamic collision behavior and applying the same compact topology contract to additional stages.
gaps.next_proof: Use Battlefield as the proven stage format, then validate dynamic line/joint callback behavior against the decomp before broadening to other stages.

gaps.decomp_phase: Anim -> IASA -> Phys -> Coll callback order and state transition tables
gaps.known_gap: Rust still has state shortcuts and partial callback groups. Throws/capture, tech/passive, wall/ceiling damage, downed, ledge, shield, and UCF interactions must be integrated in decomp-shaped batches.
gaps.next_proof: For every replay divergence, identify the exact decomp callback phase and table row before changing Rust behavior.
